messages:
Avery (CEO): Thanks everyone for joining the town hall. Opening this follow-up thread for any roadmap, positioning, or competitive questions. I'll try to respond through the day.
Priya (Head of Marketing): Quick: what's the pithy line we should use on the website to distinguish from cloud-managed endpoints? Need for homepage draft.
Avery (CEO): Use: 'A developer-first inference platform for predictable, cost-effective LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.' Focus on predictability + unified experience.
Jordan (VP Product): Also add: 'same API and tooling across deployment modes' 12 that's a big buyer worry.
Luis (Sales): Enterprise feedback: customers ask why choose us vs major cloud provider managed endpoints. Any battle-card bullets?
Avery (CEO): Battle card fundamentals: latency SLOs, cost controls (batching, quantization), private deployment/KMS, rollout & fallback policies, and observability tuned for inference.
Mei (Engineer): On roadmap: are kernel/runtime optimizations higher priority than expanding model catalog? Curious about sequencing.
Avery (CEO): Both are important. Runtime improvements have big impact on unit economics so they get strong prioritization, but model onboarding (with verified perf profiles) stays on the near-term list.
Tom (Head of Strategy): For TAM focus: are we leaning more into platform teams (enterprise) or keeping PLG-first for startups? How do we decide channel prioritization?
Avery (CEO): We'll continue PLG to drive adoption; when usage hits security/SLA thresholds we switch to a sales-assisted path. Basically usage signals expansion.
Priya (Head of Marketing): Messaging question: lead with 'production-first' or 'cost-aware'? Which should be the headline?
Avery (CEO): Lead with 'production-first' as the umbrella, then highlight 'cost-aware controls' in technical collateral.
Luis (Sales): Objection handling: 'we can self-host cheaper' 0 what should reps say?
Avery (CEO): Emphasize total cost of ownership: ops, reliability, observability, security, plus speed to value. Our private option reduces migration and compliance friction.
Mei (Engineer): Small ask: can we publish a public 'redwood-verified' performance sheet per model? Customers want numbers.
Jordan (VP Product): That's on the roadmap; we'll make an external-facing doc that summarizes latency/cost profiles and test conditions. Will post draft here.
All-Hands Bot: Slides + recording: https://redwood.internal/slides/2026-03-23-townhall (SSO)
Priya (Head of Marketing): I'll draft a one-pager and tag Jordan & Avery for edits.
Luis (Sales): I'll collect top 3 enterprise objections and share customer quotes asap.
Mei (Engineer): Can we create a channel for runtime perf alerts so infra teams can see regressions quickly?
Jordan (VP Product): Good idea 12 we'll add it to eng docs and create the channel.
Avery (CEO): Thanks all. If anyone wants a deeper follow-up, DM me or book time. I'll close this thread later today unless more follow-ups appear.
